summary.one_liner: A blog that walks through one computer science research paper at a time, summarising each paper's ideas and why they matter.
takeaways: Each post explains one CS research paper, often from systems, databases or machine learning venues such as OSDI, SIGMOD, VLDB and PODC

summary.summary: This is the front page of The Morning Paper, a blog by Adrian Colyer that presents a random walk through computer science research. Each entry picks one paper and explains its contribution in prose, with the citation (authors, venue, year) given at the top. The visible posts cover entity resolution surveys, bias in word embeddings, client-centric database isolation specifications, the Elle and Jepsen isolation checking work, 100Gbps intrusion prevention, Delos consensus, Microsoft's Helios indexing system, and learned sorting. The top post announces that this is the last edition of the blog for now.
